mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the following 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% in one month compared to previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months, or the hit rate is below 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which increases input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, which dampens consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year moving average for four consecutive months signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.
